title: Meta Ads Creator Attribution: How to Tie Ad Spend to Each Creator
summary: Learn how Meta ads creator attribution works, where platform-reported conversions overstate credit, and how to pay creators on per-creator revenue instead of blended ROAS.
body_markdown:
## What Meta Ads Creator Attribution Means (and Where the Setting Lives)


Standard Meta attribution assigns conversion credit to an ad under the selected click or view window. Creator attribution adds the identity of the creator whose content ran as that ad. To see which creator’s video is associated with an outcome, keep creator identifiers attached to the ad and reconcile Meta’s report with the store’s order data. Meta Business Help Center describes attribution settings as configurable for each ad set.


### Creator Attribution vs. Standard Meta Attribution: The Endorser Problem


Meta’s reporting answers which ad received credit under its attribution rules; it does not, by itself, establish which creator deserves payment or whether the sale was incremental. The creator is the endorser behind the video, while the ad set determines delivery and attribution settings. A useful record connects the creator handle, video or post ID, campaign, ad set, offer, and order source. Without that connection, a strong ad can generate reported conversions while the creator program still cannot assign a defensible revenue figure.


### Ad Set-Level Configuration: A Step-by-Step Walkthrough


In Ads Manager, open the campaign and ad set, review its conversion location and optimization event, then inspect Attribution Settings. Select the available click-through window that matches your measurement plan, and keep the choice consistent across comparable creator ads. Name each ad set with a stable creator identifier, such as` creator_handle_product_offer` , and carry that identifier into your reporting sheet and destination URL parameters. Before launch, confirm that the correct creator asset, landing page, event, and attribution setting appear together. Meta’s setting controls credit assignment; your naming and order reconciliation connect that credit to a creator.


### Click-Through, View-Through and Engaged-View Windows Explained


A click-through window credits an eligible conversion after someone clicks an ad within the selected period. A view-through window can credit a conversion after an ad impression without a click. Engaged-view measurement refers to qualifying video engagement before conversion, where that option is available. These windows answer different questions: did a click precede the order, did exposure precede it, or did a viewer engage with the video? Check which choices Ads Manager offers for the campaign and format rather than assuming every option applies.


Measurement signal What it captures Operational use


Click-through Conversion after an ad click within the selected window Track direct response behavior


View-through Conversion after an impression without a click Review exposure-associated credit separately


Engaged-view Conversion after qualifying video engagement, when available Assess video interaction under the applicable setting


### Why the 7-Day Click and 1-Day View Default Inflates Reported ROAS


Jon Loomer Digital identifies 7-day click and 1-day view as Meta’s default attribution setting, with 1-day and 7-day click options available at the ad set level. A longer window can associate more later purchases with an ad, while view-through credit can include buyers who did not click. That does not prove the ad caused every credited sale. Jon Loomer Digital also documents that older 28-day click, 28-day view, and 7-day view options are no longer available following Meta’s consolidated settings changes. Reacher’s[AI Creator Search](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-discovery) helps teams identify relevant creators before campaigns; it does not replace conversion measurement. AI Creator Search supports discovery, while ad and order records establish attribution.
